#TUNEL+ in lak and wt sibs between 6-9 dpf (F2P1)
```{r, echo=FALSE}
TUNELLakAge <-read.csv("/Users/cervenyk/Documents/fish data/Tectum_Hannah_Mate_collaboration/TUNEL_Hannah_requant/TectumF2P1_TUNELLakAge.csv")
View(TUNELLakAge)

### Part 1 Graph - visually inspect data and distibutions (no stats yet)
TUNELLakAge$Age<-factor(TUNELLakAge$Age, 
                        levels=c("5 dpf", "6 dpf", "7 dpf", "9 dpf"))
TUNELLakAge$Genotype<-factor(TUNELLakAge$Genotype, 
                             levels=c("WT", "lak")) 
TectumF2P1_TUNELLakAge <- ggplot(TUNELLakAge, aes(x= Genotype, y= Total))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA)+
  geom_jitter(color = "black", fill = "gray", pch=21, size = 2, alpha=0.7, width=0.3)+
  facet_wrap(~Age, strip.position = "top", scales = "fixed", nrow =1)+
  scale_x_discrete(labels=expression(WT, italic(lak)))+
  xlab("Genotype")+
  ylab("Total TUNEL+ Cells")+ 
  ylim(0,46)

print(TectumF2P1_TUNELLakAge)
```

# F2P1 Statistics
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Summary Statistics (n, mean, SD)
group_by(TUNELLakAge, Genotype, Age) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(Total, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(Total, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(Total, na.rm = TRUE))

#Group by ages
#Specify 5 dpf
F <- TUNELLakAge$Age == "5 dpf"
TUNELLakAge[F,]
#Specify 6 dpf
X <- TUNELLakAge$Age == "6 dpf"
TUNELLakAge[X,]
#Specify 7 dpf
S <- TUNELLakAge$Age == "7 dpf"
TUNELLakAge[S,]
#Specify 9 dpf
N <- TUNELLakAge$Age == "9 dpf"
TUNELLakAge[N,]

#Check Data before statistical testing
#T-test assumptions: random representative collection, appropriate sample size, normal distribution (Shapiro–Wilk test vs Q-Q plots), and homogeneity of variance
#Two-way ANOVA assumptions: normality of residuals (test with Shapiro-Wik tests and Q-Q plots) and roughly equal variance (Levene's or F-test)

## 1. Check for normal distribution
with(TUNELLakAge[F,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "lak"])) #p-value = 0.02556   *
with(TUNELLakAge[F,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "WT"])) #p-value = 0.1961
with(TUNELLakAge[X,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "lak"])) #p-value = 0.3314
with(TUNELLakAge[X,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "WT"])) #p-value = 0.09529
with(TUNELLakAge[S,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "lak"])) #p-value = 0.02668   *
with(TUNELLakAge[S,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "WT"])) #p-value = 0.06121       
with(TUNELLakAge[N,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "lak"])) #p-value = 0.6264
with(TUNELLakAge[N,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "WT"])) #p-value = 0.8734
#p-value > 0.05 implies that the distribution of the data are not significantly different from normal distribution.
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Q-Q plot for 5 dpf data
qqnorm(TUNELLakAge[F,]$Total, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(TUNELLakAge[F,]$Total, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Q-Q plot for 6 dpf data
qqnorm(TUNELLakAge[X,]$Total, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(TUNELLakAge[X,]$Total, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Q-Q plot for 7 dpf data
qqnorm(TUNELLakAge[S,]$Total, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(TUNELLakAge[S,]$Total, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Q-Q plot for 9 dpf data
qqnorm(TUNELLakAge[N,]$Total, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(TUNELLakAge[N,]$Total, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# 2. Test for equal Variance 
# F-test (var.test) is very sensitive to departure from the normal assumption. If there is doubt about normality, the better choice is to use Levene’s test or Fligner-Killeen test, which are less sensitive. Remember that Welch's t-test works with unequal variance!
var.test(Total ~ Genotype, data = TUNELLakAge[F,]) #p-value = 0.379
fligner.test(Total ~ Genotype, data = TUNELLakAge[F,]) #p-value = 0.7903
var.test(Total ~ Genotype, data = TUNELLakAge[X,]) #p-value = 0.8467
var.test(Total ~ Genotype, data = TUNELLakAge[S,]) #p-value = 0.0001537   *
fligner.test(Total ~ Genotype, data = TUNELLakAge[S,]) #p-value = 0.003101*
var.test(Total ~ Genotype, data = TUNELLakAge[N,]) #p-value = 0.09501
#p-value > 0.05 implies that the variances are not significantly different from each other
```

#Sample size is small to medium, some of datasets within the larger set are not normally distributed and/or have unequal variance so some worries about using 2-way ANOVA. Instead use generalized linear model (negative binomial) with likelihood ratio tests

```{r}
TUNELLakAge$Genotype <- factor(TUNELLakAge$Genotype, levels = c("WT", "lak"))
TUNELLakAge$Age <- factor(TUNELLakAge$Age)

# 1. Fit the Negative Binomial Model (Safely absorbs biological overdispersion)
mod_TUNELlakAgeCount <- glmmTMB(Total ~ Genotype * Age, dispformula = ~ Age, family = nbinom2, data = TUNELLakAge)

# 2. Check main effects and interaction p-values
summary(mod_TUNELlakAgeCount)

g_null <- update(mod_TUNELlakAgeCount, . ~ 1)              # check summary(g_null) still shows the dispersion model
g_add  <- update(mod_TUNELlakAgeCount, . ~ Genotype + Age)

anova(g_null, mod_TUNELlakAgeCount)      # overall LRT
anova(g_add,  mod_TUNELlakAgeCount)      # interaction LRT
AIC(mod_TUNELlakAgeCount)

#overall output that matters: mod_TUNELlakAgeCount 12 685.41 717.37 -330.70   661.41 12.778      3   0.005143 **
#(chi^2(df) = value, p = value)

# 3. Compute post-hoc pairwise slicing
# type = "response" converts log-counts back into raw counts automatically
posthoc_mod_TUNELlakAgeCount <- emmeans(mod_TUNELlakAgeCount, pairwise ~ Genotype | Age, type = "response")
summary(posthoc_mod_TUNELlakAgeCount$contrasts, adjust = "Holm", by = NULL)

posthoc_mod_TUNELlakwtALL <- emmeans(mod_TUNELlakAgeCount, pairwise ~ Age | Genotype, type = "response")
summary(posthoc_mod_TUNELlakwtALL$contrasts, adjust = "Holm", by = NULL)
```

##Now replot data with stats included
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#need to make this to input manual p-values on plot
stat_manual_lakTUNEL <-tibble::tribble(
  ~Age, ~group1,~group2,~p.adj,
  "5 dpf", "WT", "lak", 0.31,
  "6 dpf", "WT", "lak", 0.09,
  "7 dpf", "WT", "lak", 0.001,
  "9 dpf","WT","lak", 0.4142
) %>%
  mutate(
    dpf = factor(Age, levels = c("5 dpf", "6 dpf", "7 dpf", "9 dpf")),
    p.adj.signif = case_when(
      p.adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.adj < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.adj < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE          ~ "ns"
    ),
    y.position = 45   # adjust based on your error bar heights per facet
  )
#Now make the plot
TUNELLakAge$Age<-factor(TUNELLakAge$Age, 
                        levels=c("5 dpf", "6 dpf", "7 dpf", "9 dpf"))
TUNELLakAge$Genotype<-factor(TUNELLakAge$Genotype, 
                             levels=c("WT", "lak")) 
TectumF2P1_TUNELLakAge <- ggplot(TUNELLakAge, aes(x= Genotype, y= Total))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA)+
  geom_jitter(color = "black", fill = "gray", pch=21, size = 2, alpha=0.7, width=0.3)+
  facet_wrap(~Age, strip.position = "top", scales = "fixed", nrow =1)+
  scale_x_discrete(labels=expression(WT, italic(lak)))+
  xlab("Genotype")+
  ylab("Total TUNEL+ Cells")+ 
  ylim(0,46)+
    stat_pvalue_manual(stat_manual_lakTUNEL, label = "p.adj.signif", 
                     xmin = "group1", 
                     xmax = "group2",
                     y.position = "y.position")
print(TectumF2P1_TUNELLakAge)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggsave("TectumF2P1_TUNELLakAge.png", TectumF2P1_TUNELLakAge, path=NULL, 
         scale = 1, width = 14, height = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 300, limitsize = TRUE, bg=NULL)
```


#TUNEL+ in intact and one-eyed larvae between 6-9 dpf (F2P2)
```{r}
#Load data and make box plot to see distributions etc

View(RouseTUNEL)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
RouseTUNEL$dpf<-factor(RouseTUNEL$dpf,
                       levels=c("6 dpf", "7 dpf", "9 dpf"))

TectumF2P2_RouseTUNEL <- ggplot(RouseTUNEL, aes(x= Innerv, y= Ratio))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA)+
  geom_jitter(color = "black", fill = "gray", pch=21, size = 2, alpha=0.7, width=0.3)+
```

# F2P2 Statistics
```{r, echo=FALSE}

group_by(RouseTUNEL, Innerv, dpf) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(Ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(Ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(Ratio, na.rm = TRUE))
```

#Check Data before statistical testing
#T-test assumptions: random representative collection, appropriate sample size, normal distribution (Shapiro–Wilk test vs Q-Q plots), and homogeneity of variance
#Two-way ANOVA assumptions: normality of residuals (test with Shapiro-Wik tests and Q-Q plots) and roughly equal variance (Levene's or F-test)
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#group data into individual ages since that's what we're comparing and how the experiment was performed
#Specify 6 dpf
X <- RouseTUNEL$dpf == "6 dpf"
 RouseTUNEL[X,]
#Specify 7 dpf
S <- RouseTUNEL$dpf == "7 dpf"
RouseTUNEL[S,]
#Specify 9 dpf
N <- RouseTUNEL$dpf == "9 dpf"
RouseTUNEL[N,]
```
```{r}
#Check Data shape before running test/models
#Check for normality with test and Q-Q plots
with(RouseTUNEL[X,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "one-eyed"])) #p-value = 0.4394
with(RouseTUNEL[X,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "intact"])) #p-value = 0.4762
with(RouseTUNEL[S,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "one-eyed"])) #p-value = 0.9894
with(RouseTUNEL[S,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "intact"])) #p-value = 0.06636
with(RouseTUNEL[N,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "one-eyed"])) #p-value = 0.8696
with(RouseTUNEL[N,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "intact"])) #p-value = 0.04037     *
#p-value > 0.05 implies that the distribution of the data are not significantly different from normal distribution.
```
```{r}
#Q-Q plot for 6 dpf
qqnorm(RouseTUNEL[X,]$Ratio, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(RouseTUNEL[X,]$Ratio, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Q-Q plot for 7 dpf
qqnorm(RouseTUNEL[S,]$Ratio, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(RouseTUNEL[S,]$Ratio, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Q-Q plot for 9 dpf
qqnorm(RouseTUNEL[N,]$Ratio, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(RouseTUNEL[N,]$Ratio, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Variance Testing
# F-test (var.test) is very sensitive to departure from the normal assumption. If there is doubt about normality, the better choice is to use Levene’s test or Fligner-Killeen test, which are less sensitive.
# Remember that Welch's t-test robust to unequal variance 
var.test(Ratio ~ Innerv, data = RouseTUNEL[X,]) #p-value = 0.81
var.test(Ratio ~ Innerv, data = RouseTUNEL[S,]) #p-value = 0.8185
var.test(Ratio ~ Innerv, data = RouseTUNEL[N,]) #p-value = 0.6957
fligner.test(Ratio ~ Innerv, data = RouseTUNEL[N,]) #p-value = 0.9921
#p-value > 0.05 implies that the variances are not significantly different from each other
```

#Using GAM but this time with gaussian + and - response variables from the ratio; the data have mostly equal variance but not always normal and samples are unbalanced
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# 1. filter data and run model:
RouseTUNEL$Innerv <- factor(RouseTUNEL$Innerv, levels = c("intact", "one-eyed"))  
RouseTUNEL$dpf <- factor(RouseTUNEL$dpf, levels = c("6 dpf", "7 dpf", "9 dpf"))

TUNEL_innerv_model <- gam(Ratio ~ Innerv * dpf, 
                  family = gaussian(link = "identity"), 
                  data = RouseTUNEL)

# 2. Check the Model Summary
summary(TUNEL_innerv_model)
anova(gam(Ratio ~ 1, data = RouseTUNEL), TUNEL_innerv_model, test = "F")   # overall test statistic

# 3. Pairwise post-hoc tests with Bonferroni-Holm adjustment
posthoc_mod_TUNEL_innerv <- emmeans(TUNEL_innerv_model, pairwise ~ Innerv | dpf, type = "response")
summary(posthoc_mod_TUNEL_innerv$contrasts, adjust = "Holm", by = NULL)


```
